previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia was admitted for abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. She also reported transient chest discomfort, which was evaluated and ruled out as cardiac in origin. Imaging and lab studies showed no acute abnormalities, and stool tests were negative for bacterial, parasitic, and C. difficile infection, supporting a diagnosis of viral gastroenteritis. Her symptoms improved with supportive care, including fluid rehydration and symptom management. She was maintained on her home cardiac and diabetes medications throughout admission and discharged home in good condition after resolution of symptoms, with instructions for follow-up and continuation of prescribed therapies.
problems: Intestinal infection due to other organism, not elsewhere classified

Brief Hospital Course:

chest pain is unlikely to be due to unstable angina/NSTEMI.  The

statin.  Patient's hemi-body pain that woke her up in the early 
morning on two consecutive days is more consistent with 
fibromyalgia or musculoskeletal pain.  It is also possible that 
it is related to gastroparesis in the setting of uncontrolled 
diabetes and hyperglycemia, though the timing is not

not feel that we should change her regimen during this admission

Discharge Instructions:
You came to the hospital with chest pain.  Your blood tests did 
not show any evidence of heart attack and your EKG was the same 
as before.  We do not believe this pain is coming from your 
heart.  We think it might be related to your stomach or to your 
muscles or joints.  We did notice that your blood sugar was very 
high.  We consulted the ___ clinic and they recommended 
changing your insulin.  We set you up with follow up 
appointments.
.
We made the following changes to your medications:
Take your same dose of nightly Lantus 60 units, but take 20 
units of insulin before breakfast, lunch and dinner.  
Check your sugar before breakfast, lunch and dinner:  
If you are running high >150-take an extra 4units for 24 total 
units, If you are running high >200- take an extra 8 units for 
28 total units, 
If you are running high >250- take 12 extra units for 32 total 
units, If you are running high >300 take 16 extra units for a 
total of 36 total units, 
If you are over 350 take 20 extra units for 40 total units.
.
You should take Omeprazole- we checked and your insurance does 
cover this medicine.  If you have trouble, you can buy this over 
the counter, it is called Prilosec OTC.  You should take this 
medication every day.
You should take Aspirin 325 mg po daily-please buy this over the 
counter in your local pharmacy or grocery store.
.
Please keep your follow up appointment with your primary care 
doctor, your GI doctor and your cardioligist.
.

If you have new or different chest pain, worsening shortness of 
breath, fevers, chills or other symptoms that are concerning to 
you, please call your doctor or come to the emergency room.
